editorial:
Imagine finding an old cell phone in your house and realizing it starts receiving messages from someone who should not be alive. You get pulled into a creepy mystery where every text feels like a trap, and you never know if you can trust the person on the other end. The vibe is super tense and makes you look at your own gadgets with a bit of fear. It feels like a modern ghost story where technology is the bridge to something dark, keeping you on the edge of your seat the whole time.

The acting is great and the twists actually catch you off guard instead of being predictable. While some parts move a bit slow in the middle, the payoff at the end is totally worth it. If you love a good puzzle that keeps you guessing, you need to see this. It is a solid pick for a rainy weekend.
endingExplained: You find out the phone is not actually haunted by a ghost, but is being used by a killer who has been watching you for months. The final twist shows the killer was hiding in your own basement the entire time. In the last scene, you manage to trick him into a trap using the phone's loud alarm, allowing you to escape just as the police arrive to arrest him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tech-based thrillers and scary mysteries.
